transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-27
Time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM); Maya Patel, Dr. James Liu, Samira Khan, Liam O'Connor (Verdant)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on quality evaluation, recent regressions on discharge summary prompts, guardrail tuning, and next steps to validate fixes on dedicated capacity. Agreed to share prompt spreadsheets, security pack, and run a short dedicated-run for latency/cost numbers.

Topics:
- Regression observed on clinical note summarization (shortening + hallucination)
- Prompt-set scoring and threshold tuning (F1/ROUGE-ish + human labeler feedback)
- Guardrails and hallucination mitigation: tool-calling vs. post-filtering
- Dedicated pool run for throughput and cost estimation
- Security questions: KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining we'll do a quick 30 to 40 minute sync today, um mostly quality updates and next steps
[00:12] Maya Patel: yep thanks Ava, we'll run through results we saw on the latest prompt set, there were a few, uh, surprising regressions after the last model flip
[00:22] Diego Martinez: quick context, last week we switched from redwood-3b-v2 to redwood-3b-v3 quantized, with the new kernel selector--the idea was slightly cheaper tokens but some mismatch on longer contexts
[00:36] Dr. James Liu: right so what we saw is the discharge summaries are now trimming important follow-up instructions, like meds and transfer notes, and in a couple cases adding in, um, predicted meds that weren't documented
[00:49] Samira Khan: and to add, our automated scoring dropped ~6 points on the rouge-lite metric we run, and the human raters flagged hallucination in 8% of samples
[01:03] Diego Martinez: ok that's consistent with an alignment/temperature or beam change, could be the kv cache pruning we enabled, or the batching profile causing truncated contexts, we should verify the seq len and prompt prefix isn't being truncated in the pipeline
[01:20] Liam O'Connor: from security side nothing new, just want confirmation that logs are routed to our syslog endpoint and KMS is used for keys in the private deployment
[01:30] Ava Chen: absolutely, we'll share the infra diagram and the KMS notes. note re: logging, the audit logs for PII access are retained 90 days by default for this POC, we can increase if needed
[01:44] Maya Patel: ok thanks. For the scoring, we attached the prompt set CSV in the board but Diego can you walk us through the failing examples?
[01:55] Diego Martinez: sure, um i'll share my screen--the first cluster is on 'post-op discharge summary' prompts. example 1, input had explicit med reconciliation section but model dropped the entire section after the new quantized runtime, so we see omission errors. example 4 actually invented a follow-up called 'beta blocker adjustment' which wasn't in the notes, that's a hallucination
[02:17] Dr. James Liu: that's the risky one for us, hallucinations around med changes are a non-starter
[02:23] Diego Martinez: agreed. a few action items we propose: 1) pin to the previous model variant for the med-critical prompts as a temporary canary; 2) add a guardrail filter that checks for missing sections and flags for human review; 3) run a re-calibrated scoring pass with adjusted temperature and sampling params
[02:38] Maya Patel: quick Q - pinning affects our latency/cost targets?
[02:42] Ava Chen: pinning to the non-quantized model will increase token cost by ~18-25% from our initial numbers, but we can do per-route pinning so only the med-critical route uses it
[02:54] Samira Khan: that could work, we'll likely want per-intent routing. we can send over the top 10 intents and which ones require strict recall
[03:05] Diego Martinez: perfect. Also re: guardrails, we can deploy a lightweight post-filter that enforces presence of required headings and runs a simple entity-coverage check. if it fails we return a 'requires human review' tag; this is much cheaper than adding deterministic tool-calling for every call
[03:23] Dr. James Liu: tool-calling might still be necessary for high risk flows, e.g., if the model is unsure about medication changes, call a structured extractor or the EHR to confirm
[03:33] Diego Martinez: yeah we recommend a hybrid: post-filter for 90% of cases, and tool-call / structured extraction for the top 2-3 highest risk flows
[03:44] Maya Patel: ok makes sense. what's the plan for re-evaluating after these changes? timeline?
[03:48] Ava Chen: short term: Diego will export failing examples today/tomorrow, we'll push a guardrail rule and a model pin for med-critical routes. then Verdant runs a 48-hour dedicated pool test next week to get latency/cost numbers. after that we reconvene to review updated scoring
[04:02] Samira Khan: about the dedicated run, can you remind me if we need a config change in our VPC or is this handled by Redwood Dedicated?
[04:09] Diego Martinez: Redwood Dedicated will sit in a customer-VPC peering config for this POC; we will provide an infra template. For onboarding we need your network CIDR and the firewall rules; Priya will follow up with the onboarding doc link
[04:22] Priya Rao: yes i'll drop the onboarding link in the notes and cc the infra team, link: https://redwood.ai/poc/onboarding (note: sample link, internal doc)
[04:31] Liam O'Connor: Regarding encryption, we need confirmation that keys are customer-managed KMS, HSM ok?
[04:36] Ava Chen: yes for Private we support customer-managed KMS; HSM is an add-on for enterprise. i'll include options in the security pack we share
[04:45] Maya Patel: any mention of competitors in your eval? we ran a quick side-by-side with Anthropic on a tiny set and got different hallucination patterns
[04:54] Diego Martinez: we did a quick benchmark vs Anthropic base on our dev set; Anthropic model was slightly better on instruction sticking but worse on long-context recall. i'll include the brief comparison in the spreadsheet but it's not a formal benchmark
[05:05] Ava Chen: couple of notes on scoring - you mentioned rouge-lite and human labelers, can you remind us of the pass/fail thresholds?
[05:12] Maya Patel: currently: automated threshold is 82% on our rouge-lite and human acceptance > 90% across 50 sampled records; anything below triggers hold-for-review
[05:21] Diego Martinez: ok we should add a per-intent threshold in the spreadsheet so the canary routing is automatic. we'll add that column
[05:30] Dr. James Liu: on hallucination detection, can the post-filter check factual consistency against the EHR content?
[05:36] Diego Martinez: yes, the post-filter can do a surface-level cross-check for entities and dates; for deep fact-checking we'd recommend the tool call to the structured extractor which has canonical EHR fields
[05:46] Samira Khan: about the prompt set, we noticed some prompts include overly-long context, could that be amplifying truncation?
[05:52] Diego Martinez: yes long context increases chance of kv cache pruning; we'll add guidance to trim unnecessary history and use summarized context for repeated intents
[06:03] Maya Patel: good. Any blockers on your side?
[06:07] Ava Chen: none critical, just need the traffic profile CSV and top intents from Samira, and Diego needs to export failing examples. we'll also share the security pack
[06:15] Samira Khan: i'll get that over by Friday, and we'll aim to kick the dedicated 48 hour run Monday if firewall rules are set
[06:23] Priya Rao: action items recap: Diego will export failing examples; Ava will share SOC2 + KMS notes; Samira will send traffic profile and top intents; we'll schedule the dedicated run once network details are confirmed
[06:38] Maya Patel: thanks all. any other questions?
[06:42] Liam O'Connor: none from security; i'll review the pack when it's sent and follow up if anything missing
[06:48] Ava Chen: great, we'll target next check-in same time next week, unless the dedicated run finishes earlier. thanks everyone

References & shared artifacts:
- Prompt set CSV (attached in CRM)
- Scoring spreadsheet with rouge-lite and human labels (link to internal sheet)
- Security pack (SOC2, KMS notes, infra diagram)

End of transcript
